clf-med-051.text: A network analysis revealed that a sub-network needs to block all traffic coming from a known malicious IP range, and the team wants to apply this denial rule to the sub-network layer, evaluating the rules in numerical order. Security Groups and Network ACLs, why the Network ACL is the right choice for this case?
options: Because Network ACLs encrypt blocked traffic before discarding it
Because Network ACLs support explicit Deny rules at the subnet boundary, while Security Groups use Allow rules at the resource interface level
Because Security Groups can control only outbound traffic, not inbound traffic
Because Network ACLs are stateful and automatically remember allowed connections
clf-med-051.explanation: Security Groups use Allow rules and operate on resource network interfaces, while Network ACLs operate at the subnet boundary and support numbered Allow and Deny rules, which makes them suitable for explicitly blocking a known IP range.
clf-med-051.hint: One VPC firewall works with Allow rules at the resource interface; the other supports numbered Allow and Deny rules at the subnet boundary.
optionRationales: Security Groups use Allow rules and operate on resource network interfaces, while Network ACLs operate at the subnet boundary and support numbered Allow and Deny rules, which makes them suitable for explicitly blocking a known IP range.
Network ACLs are stateless, while Security Groups are stateful. The statement reverses their connection-state behavior.
Security Groups can control both inbound and outbound traffic; the relevant limitation here is that they do not support explicit Deny rules.
Network ACLs allow or deny packets based on rules and do not encrypt network traffic.

clf-med-052.text: Before launching an application, a hired security consultancy wants to perform penetration testing against the customer's EC2 instances and RDS databases on AWS. What is AWS's position on customer penetration testing?
options: All penetration testing is prohibited on AWS because it may affect other customers
Invasion tests are allowed without prior approval for a list of authorized services, such as EC2, RDS, CloudFront and API Gateway, as long as it respects the testing policy of the AWS
Every penetration test requires formal written AWS approval 90 days in advance
Penetration testing can be performed only by AWS Support engineers
clf-med-052.explanation: AWS permits customers to perform penetration testing against specified authorized services without submitting a prior approval request, provided the testing follows AWS security testing policies and does not include prohibited activities such as unauthorized denial-of-service testing.
clf-med-052.hint: AWS publishes a list of services against which customers can test their own resources without requesting advance permission, subject to policy restrictions.
optionRationales: AWS permits customers to perform penetration testing against specified authorized services without submitting a prior approval request, provided the testing follows AWS security testing policies and does not include prohibited activities such as unauthorized denial-of-service testing.
AWS does allow security testing of a customer's own resources on authorized services; there is no blanket prohibition on all penetration testing.
For the authorized services covered by the policy, the former general advance-authorization process is not required.
Customers or security providers hired by them can test authorized resources under the policy; AWS Support does not have to conduct the penetration test.

clf-med-053.text: An administrator wants continuous visibility into whether an S3 bucket, IAM role, or SQS queue is accessible to external entities such as other accounts or anonymous users by analyzing resource policies for unintended sharing. Which AWS capability provides this analysis?
options: AWS Resource Groups
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon Macie
IAM Access Analyzer
clf-med-053.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes supported resource policies to identify resources shared with principals outside the account or organization and helps surface unintended external access.
clf-med-053.hint: Think of the IAM analyzer designed to answer which resources in the account are accessible from outside the intended trust boundary.
optionRationales: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes supported resource policies to identify resources shared with principals outside the account or organization and helps surface unintended external access.
AWS CloudTrail records API activity that has occurred but does not primarily analyze resource policies to identify externally shared resources.
Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3 but does not analyze access policies across IAM roles, queues, and other resource types for external sharing.
AWS Resource Groups helps organize resources by attributes and tags and does not perform security-policy exposure analysis.

clf-med-054.text: A multinational company organizes AWS accounts in AWS Organizations OUs named Production, Development, and Sandbox. Governance attaches one SCP to the organization root and another SCP specifically to the Sandbox OU. How do the SCPs affect accounts in the Sandbox OU?
options: Only the root SCP applies because SCPs cannot be attached to OUs
Sandbox accounts are subject to the combined effect of SCPs inherited from the root and SCPs attached to their OU
SCPs do not affect Sandbox accounts because they apply only to the management account
Only the Sandbox OU SCP applies because policies closer to the account replace root policies
clf-med-054.explanation: SCPs follow the AWS Organizations hierarchy. Member accounts are affected by applicable policies attached at the root and OU levels above them, so restrictions inherited from higher levels continue to apply lower in the tree.
clf-med-054.hint: Think of hierarchical inheritance: a restriction applied higher in the organization remains relevant to accounts in descendant OUs.
optionRationales: SCPs follow the AWS Organizations hierarchy. Member accounts are affected by applicable policies attached at the root and OU levels above them, so restrictions inherited from higher levels continue to apply lower in the tree.
SCPs do not replace one another based on proximity; restrictions can combine through the organization hierarchy.
SCPs can be attached to the root, OUs, and individual accounts, so OU-level policy attachment is a normal governance pattern.
SCPs are designed to limit permissions in member accounts; the management account is not constrained by SCPs in the same way as member accounts.

clf-med-055.text: A company's website is behind Amazon CloudFront. The security team wants to understand how AWS Shield Standard and AWS WAF differ in protecting the site. Which distinction is correct?
options: The Shield Standard automatically mitigates volumetric DDoS attacks of network and transport (layers 3 and 4), while the WAF filters malicious requirements in the application layer (chamber 7), as SQL injection
Shield Standard protects the application layer and AWS WAF protects the network and transport layers
They provide the same capability, but AWS WAF is simply the paid version of Shield Standard
Shield Standard works only when AWS WAF has already been purchased and configured
clf-med-055.explanation: The services are complementary. AWS Shield Standard provides automatic baseline DDoS protection, while AWS WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS requests according to configurable web-application rules.
clf-med-055.hint: Separate the attacks by layer: volumetric packet floods versus malicious but well-formed HTTP requests.
optionRationales: The services are complementary. AWS Shield Standard provides automatic baseline DDoS protection, while AWS WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS requests according to configurable web-application rules.
It's reversed: the Shield act in the layers of infrastructure (3 and 4) and the WAF in the application layer (7).
They are different complementary services. The advanced paid Shield tier is AWS Shield Advanced, not AWS WAF.
AWS Shield Standard protection is provided automatically for AWS customers and does not require AWS WAF to be configured first.

clf-med-056.text: A media company stores millions of objects in Amazon S3 and, for privacy compliance, needs to discover automatically whether objects contain sensitive personal data such as national identification numbers, payment-card data, or credentials and receive findings when such information appears in inappropriate locations. Which service uses machine learning and pattern matching for this discovery and classification?
options: Amazon Macie
AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Inspector
clf-med-056.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and help classify sensitive data stored in Amazon S3, supporting data-security and privacy programs.
clf-med-056.hint: Think of the AWS machine-learning-powered data security service specialized in discovering sensitive information in S3.
optionRationales: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and help classify sensitive data stored in Amazon S3, supporting data-security and privacy programs.
Amazon Inspector identifies software vulnerabilities and network exposure in supported compute workloads rather than sensitive personal data inside S3 objects.
AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual data-preparation service for analytics and is not primarily a security service for sensitive-data discovery.
Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and videos for visual content and is not a service for classifying textual sensitive data inside general S3 objects.

clf-med-057.text: When designing security for a new application, an architect decides that every microservice will receive only the permissions strictly necessary for its job and that permissions will be reviewed and reduced periodically based on actual usage. Which security principle is being applied?
options: AWS Shared Responsibility Model
Environment isolation
Principle of least privilege
Defense in depth
clf-med-057.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the minimum permissions required to perform a task and reviewing those permissions over time, which is a central IAM and security best practice.
clf-med-057.hint: The principle is summarized by the phrase: grant only what is necessary, and nothing more.
optionRationales: Least privilege means granting only the minimum permissions required to perform a task and reviewing those permissions over time, which is a central IAM and security best practice.
The AWS Shared Responsibility Model divides security responsibilities between AWS and the customer and does not define the minimum permission set for each identity.
Defense in depth means using multiple layers of security controls; the scenario specifically describes minimizing permissions granted to each service.
Separating environments can reduce blast radius but is not the principle governing minimum identity permissions.

clf-med-058.text: A team discovers that traffic between its EC2 instances and Amazon S3 travels through a NAT Gateway, creating unnecessary cost and security concerns. The team wants the traffic to remain private on the AWS network by using a VPC feature designed for private service access. Which resource meets this objective?
options: An additional Internet Gateway dedicated to S3
A second NAT Gateway in another Availability Zone
AWS Direct Connect between subnets in the same VPC
A VPC Endpoint, specifically a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3
clf-med-058.explanation: An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint enables resources in a VPC to access S3 without requiring an Internet Gateway or NAT Gateway for that traffic, keeping the service path on the AWS network and avoiding NAT data-processing charges for those requests.
clf-med-058.hint: There is a VPC feature designed as a private path to supported AWS services without internet or NAT traversal.
optionRationales: An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint enables resources in a VPC to access S3 without requiring an Internet Gateway or NAT Gateway for that traffic, keeping the service path on the AWS network and avoiding NAT data-processing charges for those requests.
An Internet Gateway provides public internet connectivity and would not create the private service path required here.
AWS Direct Connect links an on-premises network to AWS and is not the mechanism for connecting VPC subnets privately to Amazon S3.
Another NAT Gateway would add redundancy to the NAT path but would not eliminate NAT processing or provide the dedicated private service endpoint.

clf-med-059.text: A technology director wants a service that helps establish and centrally govern a multi-account AWS environment from the beginning: create new accounts in a standardized automated way, apply preventive and detective governance controls based on best practices, and monitor compliance through a unified experience built on AWS Organizations. Which service provides this ready-made governance capability?
options: AWS Systems Manager
Amazon Connect
AWS Control Tower
AWS Organizations by itself
clf-med-059.explanation: AWS Control Tower automates setup and governance of a multi-account landing zone, supports standardized account provisioning, and applies governance controls while building on AWS Organizations.
clf-med-059.hint: Think of the AWS control tower that orchestrates account provisioning and governance controls on top of Organizations.
optionRationales: AWS Control Tower automates setup and governance of a multi-account landing zone, supports standardized account provisioning, and applies governance controls while building on AWS Organizations.
AWS Organizations provides the account hierarchy, SCPs, and consolidated billing foundation, while Control Tower adds opinionated landing-zone automation and centralized governance capabilities.
AWS Systems Manager focuses on operational management of resources such as automation, patching, and inventory rather than standardized multi-account landing-zone governance.
Amazon Connect is a cloud contact-center service and is unrelated to AWS account governance.

clf-med-060.text: An engineering company runs scientific simulations that require very high sustained CPU performance with only moderate memory consumption. Which Amazon EC2 instance-family category is the best fit?
options: Compute Optimized instances (C family)
Storage Optimized instances (I family)
Burstable General Purpose instances (T family)
Memory Optimized instances (R family)
clf-med-060.explanation: Compute Optimized instances provide a high ratio of compute power to memory and are designed for compute-intensive workloads such as scientific modeling, media processing, and high-performance application servers.
clf-med-060.hint: Match the workload's bottleneck, sustained CPU processing, to the EC2 family category optimized for compute.
optionRationales: Compute Optimized instances provide a high ratio of compute power to memory and are designed for compute-intensive workloads such as scientific modeling, media processing, and high-performance application servers.
Memory Optimized R-family instances emphasize large amounts of memory for memory-intensive workloads rather than primarily CPU-bound simulations.
Burstable T-family instances are suited to workloads with intermittent CPU bursts, not sustained heavy CPU utilization.
Storage Optimized I-family instances emphasize high local storage IOPS and throughput rather than raw CPU performance.
